acv.quote: We proposed six hundred K a year.

data.reason: Lost to Adyen on the store side. Angela, the COO, signed after we offered a partner for installs and never showed a till return. Tom credits the web side, but stores decided it.

trigger.action: Lead with returning an online order at a store, not channel talk.
trigger.why: Angela, the COO, reportedly watched the returns queue after stores couldn't see online orders.
trigger.quote: The store couldn't see the online order

decider.action: Tell the COO one vendor answers for both stores and web.
decider.why: Angela signed with Adyen. Tom met her once, at the kickoff, and worked mostly with Raj, the CTO.
decider.quote: I don't want two vendors pointing at each other.

competitor.action: Show our store rollout experience and name retailers running our tills.
competitor.why: Raj told Tom that Adyen brought a store rollout team. Afterwards, 11 of their 14 questions were about stores.
competitor.quote: they came in with a retail team, people who'd done store rollouts

message.action: Replace the 'line has disappeared' slide with a step-by-step till return.
message.why: Bev, head of store operations, dismissed the slide and asked how a return works at the till.

proof.action: Add a retailer story buyers can call, with real rollout dates and installs.
proof.why: Angela asked to talk to the fashion retailer in our case study, and we couldn't arrange a call in time.

words.action: Say 'the tills' and 'one customer, one basket', not 'point of sale'.
words.why: Bev used this phrase every time, and they never said 'unified commerce'.
words.quote: One system for the tills and the website.
